title: Step 63-G Payment handoff, provider callback bridge and authoritative order outcome
description: HIGH-risk Step 63-G. Productionize payment initiation, provider callback handoff, authoritative status/verify recovery and Order Outcome without fabricating success. Ambiguous initiation without a signed payment handoff fails closed: authoritative Order payment state blocks a duplicate payment until the prior outcome is terminal or recoverable. Real provider enablement and production secrets remain deferred to Step 74.

dependencies.evidence: PR #309 protected workflow_dispatch 37191884831; merge job 111405640903 SUCCESS; exact-SHA postmerge 111405690958 SUCCESS; terminal Lock release comment 5978521969.

acceptance_criteria.description: Checkout Review creates the order idempotently and then initiates payment using the server-only Checkout token and a stable idempotency key. It never fabricates payment success when initiation is unavailable or ambiguous.

A Storefront provider-callback bridge receives the provider GET callback, sends callback state only server-to-server to the canonical backend callback operation, and redirects to /payment/return without carrying callback state or secrets forward.

Payment return is bound to an HttpOnly HMAC-signed handoff tied to the Checkout token and determines result only from authoritative payment status/verify. Query parameters cannot select an unrelated payment.

Order outcome loads the authoritative order and bound payment, displays paid/pending/failed/refund-required states without inference, and allows a new payment attempt only after authoritative status proves the prior attempt is terminal or no prior handoff exists.

If initiation becomes ambiguous before a signed payment handoff exists, Order Outcome fails closed. A pending/authorized/paid/refund state on the authoritative Order blocks any fresh payment attempt; only unpaid/failed/cancelled order state may recover without a prior handoff.
Provider enablement remains fail-closed by default. No merchant secret, production provider activation, provider infrastructure change or Step 74 production integration is introduced.

Persian RTL, bidi isolation for references, 44px targets, visible focus and responsive reflow are present. No payment/checkout credential or callback state enters browser storage or user-visible diagnostics.

Canonical completion requires exact-head Canonical CI, Phase A, Storefront Quality, CodeQL Security, deterministic Review, exact-artifact Human Gate, ACTIVE Lock, protected merge, exact-SHA postmerge verification and terminal Lock release.

The Step 63-C foundation, Step 63-E identity and Step 63-F fulfillment predecessor verifiers are transition-aware: they preserve their original invariants while accepting either the original payment/outcome placeholders or the atomic production successor runtime introduced by Step 63-G. No security, credential, identity or fulfillment assertion is removed.

payment_provider_boundary.callback_bridge_requirement: PAYMENT_CALLBACK_BASE_URL must resolve to the Storefront origin when a browser-return provider flow is enabled so /payments/:paymentId/callback can proxy state server-to-server and return to /payment/return.
payment_provider_boundary.ambiguous_initiation_recovery: No backend mutation in Step 63-G. If browser/server transport loses the initiated payment_id, Storefront reads authoritative Order payment_status and blocks duplicate initiation for pending/authorized/paid/refund states; operator/customer recovery remains fail-closed until the backend exposes a safe payment identity.
